faehigkeiten.grund: Auslieferung wird je Abruf neu zusammengesetzt (adswizz vergibt je Abruf eine listeningSessionID, AIS leitet ueber hash_redirect um, Last-Modified liegt nur 2 s vor dem Abruf, Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst simplecastaudio.com) - Byte-Offsets veralten (bei dynamischer Auslieferung sofort, gemessen 19.08.2026) und die Zeitachse verschiebt sich mit (eine Folge war 57 s kuerzer als 3,5 h zuvor), deshalb sind auch Sprungmarken in Sekunden unsicher

einzeiler: Sara Bareilles talks about grief, fertility struggles, and her new album Good Grief.
kurzfassung: Rachel Martin welcomes singer and actress Sara Bareilles to play the card-based conversation game Wildcard. They discuss grief, the inspiration behind her album Good Grief, and her experiences with fertility clinics. They also explore personal growth, letting go of control, and finding humor in life's challenges.
stichpunkte: Sara Bareilles discusses her latest album Good Grief, which was heavily shaped by the loss of close friends.
She reflects on the intense emotional experience of moving in with her husband and living in New York.
Bareilles shares her challenging journey through fertility treatments and waiting rooms.
She describes the deep impact of grief and mortality, noting how death has been an incredible teacher.
The conversation covers her creative process, including a spontaneous songwriting moment prompted by grief.
Bareilles talks about her relationship with the validation of others and her shift toward trusting a small circle of loved ones.
She shares thoughts on aging, embracing mystery over certainty, and finding curiosity about the future.
The episode concludes with a nostalgic memory of her father driving her to school.

clips.hook: A memory of a mother weeping on shag carpet
clips.text: Recalling a childhood memory of her mother crying on the basement floor during a family move, symbolizing the deep emotional attachment to physical spaces.

clips.hook: Writing a song for a lifelong friend
clips.text: Explaining the background of a deeply personal song written for a college friend and long-time manager who passed away from cancer.

clips.hook: Composing music in a fertility clinic waiting room
clips.text: Describing how an entire song was written while sitting in the rows of chairs at a fertility clinic.

clips.hook: Saying a prayer to avoid selling out
clips.text: Recalling a moment of fear regarding industry pressure where a quick prayer helped refocus on the true love of songwriting.

clips.hook: Making peace with death but still wanting more time
clips.text: Discussing the complex acceptance of mortality while admitting a strong desire to stay and experience more of life.

beschreibung:
“Being a human is so complicated for so many reasons,” Sara Bareilles tells Rachel. That’s why she’s trying to show more grace for both herself and others these days. In Sara’s new album and documentary, both titled “Good Grief,” she’s processing the loss of dear friends, and her struggles with fertility. She also tells Rachel about becoming an unapologetic crier, and outgrowing low rise jeans.
